note: The High cache path into `release.yml` was judged overstated: its default-branch writers are pushes to main or wip/** by writers, fork pull_request runs write only their own scope, so it holds at Medium at most; the High `pgxn/matrix-action@v0` path in `ci.yml` was judged overstated: the job holds no secret and the repository default token is read-only (the `GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions` block of a recent run log), so a compromised action only runs code on the runner, Medium at most. Corrected after reading the workflows: the assessment named only insiders as writers, but a push or dispatch run whose job is entered through an unauthorized mutable action (a High dependency path of the same repository) also writes the default-branch cache the release restores, so the cache path holds at the High ceiling of that writer, not at Medium. No job here declares cache-mode, so GitHub keeps the cache of every low-trust run read-only and grants no job cache write: ISSUE-705 is silent and no cache path exists, so the cache ceiling admits none.
